title: Payload Handling & Coordination
contentStatus: Built per Content Principles (60% pass, terminology + notes). Handshake signal specifics pending SME confirmation (L2 operator-level detail).

sections.title: Why Payload Handling Matters
learningObjectives: Understand the range of payload configurations MoRo supports
Recognize that payload type affects operational procedure
sections.content: MoRo isn't a single fixed tool - it supports multiple payload configurations (conveyor, cobot interface, towing, lifting, and lift-and-rotate), each suited to different material handling needs. The configuration in use directly affects what you need to check and how you interact with a unit during operation.

keyTerms.note: The specific attachment or module fitted to MoRo for handling a given type of material transfer.
Automated machine tools controlled by programmed instructions, commonly loaded and unloaded by MoRo in machine tending applications.

sections.title: Attachment and Setup
learningObjectives: Understand the general process of confirming a payload attachment
Know why attachment verification matters before mission assignment
sections.content: Before a mission involving material transfer begins, the payload attachment must be confirmed secure and correctly configured for the task. An improperly seated or mismatched attachment risks dropped material or a failed handoff mid-mission. The specific verification steps per attachment type will be confirmed and added once validated against DiFacto's equipment documentation.

sections.title: Handshake Signals
learningObjectives: Understand the concept of a handshake in machine coordination
Recognize the operator-level implication of handshake states
sections.content: When MoRo coordinates with another machine - loading from or delivering to a CNC station, for example - the two systems exchange a handshake: a sequence of signals confirming readiness, completion, and any error state, so neither system acts before the other is genuinely ready. At the operator level, you don't need to manage this sequence directly, but you should recognize when a handshake has stalled (the exchange pauses and doesn't progress) as a signal worth flagging. Exact signal states and sequence detail are being confirmed with DiFacto's engineering team.

keyTerms.note: A signal exchange between two coordinating systems confirming readiness, completion, or error state before an action proceeds.

sections.title: Safety With Loaded Payloads
learningObjectives: Understand how a loaded payload changes MoRo's operating behavior
Know the additional awareness required around a loaded unit
sections.content: A loaded MoRo behaves differently from an empty one - weight distribution shifts its center of gravity, which affects stopping behavior and stability, particularly with the lift or lift-and-rotate configurations. Give loaded units additional clearance, and never attempt to adjust or steady a load manually while MoRo is in motion.

sections.title: Coordinating With Fixed Machines
learningObjectives: Understand the general principle of timing in machine-to-machine handoffs
Recognize the operator's role during a coordinated handoff
sections.content: When MoRo interacts with a fixed machine - loading a CNC, receiving from a conveyor - timing matters. The systems are designed to coordinate automatically via handshake signals, but an operator present during a handoff should confirm both systems show a ready or completing state before assuming the exchange succeeded, rather than walking away as soon as MoRo appears to stop.

sections.title: Troubleshooting Payload Issues
learningObjectives: Recognize common categories of payload-related issues
sections.content: Common payload issues include misalignment during attachment, a handshake that doesn't progress, or a load that appears unstable. As with mission failures, diagnosis at this level isn't expected - note the issue, don't attempt to force a misaligned attachment into place, and escalate to your supervisor or the point of contact for MoRo operations.

questions.question: Does MoRo support a single fixed payload type?
options: Yes, one configuration for all tasks
No - it supports multiple configurations (conveyor, cobot, towing, lift, lift-and-rotate)
questions.feedback: Correct. MoRo supports multiple payload configurations suited to different handling needs.

questions.question: What is a handshake in the context of machine coordination?
options: A signal exchange confirming readiness, completion, or error state between systems
questions.feedback: Correct. A handshake is a coordination signal exchange, not a physical action.

questions.question: How does a loaded payload affect MoRo's operating behavior?
options: It shifts center of gravity, affecting stopping behavior and stability
questions.feedback: Correct. Weight distribution from a loaded payload affects stability and stopping behavior.

questions.question: During a coordinated handoff with a fixed machine, what should an operator confirm?
options: Nothing - the systems handle it automatically with no verification needed
That both systems show a ready or completing state before assuming success
That the machine is turned off
questions.feedback: Correct. Confirming state before assuming success avoids incomplete handoffs going unnoticed.

questions.question: If a payload attachment seems misaligned, what should you do?
options: Note the issue and escalate rather than forcing it
Ignore it and proceed with the mission
questions.feedback: Correct. Forcing a misaligned attachment risks damage; escalation is the correct response.
